title: Notice v1 (an owner notification)

source.description: the sending project (its ST project name)

kind.description: alert: something happened; todo: the owner should do something; question: an agent asks (answered in Aico, needs open with ?ask=); info: for the record

detail.description: longer text for the item's page and card

key.description: what this is about: a repeat of an open notice's key from the same source stays quiet for cooldown

open.description: the item's own place; Open goes there

command.description: one command the owner may run (Copy)

push.description: phone: ask for the phone too; tray: the desktop only. The phone is reached only with an interrupt reason (or Aico's own morning digest); a phone request without one stays in the tray. Default: phone when there is a reason, else tray

interrupt.description: why the owner is interrupted on the phone: an agent or approval truly waits on them (needs-you), a security event, a backup failing or long overdue (data-risk), an always-on host or service down for a while (outage), or a reminder they set. Severity does not route to the phone; everything without a reason stays in the tray and the morning digest. The stored notice carries phone_reason, one line saying why it reached the phone

machine.description: the machine this is about; Aico fills in the sender's machine when it's left out

project.description: the project this is about; Aico fills in the source when it's left out

lab.description: the machine this is about is a lab machine (the OmniNull hub's rule); it files under its own type in Settings

cooldown.description: seconds a repeat of the key stays quiet (default 3600)

expires.description: seconds after sending when it ends by itself (a time-bound announcement): it leaves the tray and its page says it ended

if_ignored.description: one line: what happens if the owner does nothing (shown with the item)

description: What a sender gives Aico to tell the owner something: notice contract v1, the object the OmniNull hub and local senders already use. aico-web hands its own notices (asks, shares, captures) to its Notifier in process; other programs on this machine POST one on loopback (POST /api/notices, `aico notify`); the OmniNull hub POSTs notices and its own Status rows to POST /api/ominull/push with its key. packages/notify checks it (notice.ts) and replays contracts/notice-fixtures.json. A notice that asks the owner something (kind question or todo, or an alert offering expected/not-expected) shows in Needs you as a Tether ask. An OmniNull alert names the hub's alert ids in its key ('alerts:<id>[,<id>...]'); the owner's 'That was me' sends those ids to the hub's verdict route.
